inaccuracy.text: Not bad, Commander, but there was a sharper path. {bestMove} was a touch better.
A small wobble. Nothing lost but a little momentum. Consider {bestMove} next time.
Close! The idea is sound, but {bestMove} kept more pressure on.

mistake.text: Hmm, that costs us {loss}. {bestMove} would have kept things steady.
A misstep, Commander. Let me show you why {bestMove} was stronger.
That one lets {loss} slip away. Better to learn it now than in a real battle.

blunder.text: Ah. That move gives away {loss}. Shall we take it back and try {bestMove}?
Steady, Commander. That one hurts. {bestMove} was the move to find.
A big slip! It happens to every hero. Undo, breathe, and look again.

good.text: Good move, Commander! Solid and sensible.
Nicely done. That keeps our position healthy.
A good, honest move. I approve heartily.
Well played. You're getting the hang of this.

best.text: That's exactly the move I'd have chosen. Eventually.
The best move on the board! Splendid work, Commander.
Perfect! There was nothing better to play.

brilliant.text: Brilliant! A move worthy of song. I'm composing it now.
Remarkable, Commander! Few would dare that, and it works!
Oh, that's beautiful. A sacrifice with a real plan behind it. Bravo!

fork.text: Careful! Their {attacker} can jump to {square} and attack two pieces at once.
That allows a fork: their {attacker} hits your {target} and another piece together.
Watch {square}. From there one enemy piece attacks two of ours, and we can only save one.
A fork! Your {piece} attacks two pieces at once. They can't save both.

pin.text: Your {target} is pinned. If it moves, the piece behind it is exposed.
Their {attacker} pins your {target} against a bigger piece. It's stuck for now.
Mind the pin on {square}. That {target} can't move without losing something worse.
Lovely pin! Their piece can't move without exposing a more valuable one.

skewer.text: A skewer! Their {attacker} hits your {target}, and when it moves, the piece behind falls.
Your {target} and the piece behind it are lined up. Their {attacker} can use that.
A skewer! The big piece must step aside, and the one behind is ours.

hanging.text: Your {piece} on {square} is undefended. Their {attacker} can simply take it.
Nobody is guarding your {piece} on {square}. Let's give it a friend or move it.
That leaves your {piece} on {square} all alone. Free pieces are everyone's favourite.

backRank.text: Our back rank is weak! The king has no escape square, so a rook or queen could mate.
Watch the back rank. Give the king a little window, like a pawn step in front of it.
Back rank strike! Their king is trapped behind its own pawns.

missedCapture.text: You could have taken their {target} on {square} for free. Always look for loose pieces!
There was a free {target} on {square}. Before each move, check what you can capture.
{bestMove} would have won {loss}. Their {target} was unguarded.

allowsMate.text: Careful! After that, they can checkmate. {bestMove} keeps our king safe.
That move lets them mate us. Let's take it back and guard the king first.
Danger! Their {attacker} now has a checkmate coming. Shall we undo it?

missedMate.text: You had a checkmate! It started with {bestMove}. Look at checks first!
So close! {bestMove} led to mate. Next time, try every check.
Victory was there, starting with {bestMove}. Checks, captures, threats, in that order.

trappedPiece.text: Your {piece} on {square} has no safe squares left. They can win it now.
That {piece} is boxed in. Pieces need room to breathe, just like heroes.
You trapped their {target}! It has nowhere safe to go.

discovered.text: Look out! When their piece moves, the {attacker} behind it attacks your {target}.
A hidden attack: one enemy piece steps aside and their {attacker} strikes.
A discovered attack! One piece moves and the one behind it strikes. Sneaky!

threat.text: Before you move: their {attacker} is eyeing your {target} on {square}.
Watch out, Commander. They're threatening your {target}. What shall we do?
Their last move had an idea behind it. Can you spot what their {attacker} wants?

hangingPiece.text: Your {piece} on {square} is unguarded. Maybe give it some company?
Quick check: is your {piece} on {square} safe? I count no defenders.

castleSoon.text: Keep me in the middle much longer and I'll get nervous. Shall we castle?
Castling tucks the king away and brings a rook into play. Two good deeds in one.

developPieces.text: Some of our knights and bishops are still at home. Let's bring them out!
Every piece wants to join the adventure. Develop them before you attack.

controlCentre.text: The centre squares are prime real estate. A pawn or knight there helps a lot.
Pieces in the centre see more of the board. Try to claim it early.

kingSafety.text: My guard looks a little thin. Perhaps shore up the pawns around the king?
Their pieces are gathering near our king. Be careful moving the pawns there.

endgameKingActive.text: It's the endgame! The king can fight now. Bring me forward. I'm ready. Mostly.
With fewer pieces about, the king is a strong piece. March it toward the centre.

wellPlayed.text: A fine game, Commander! Your moves were clear and brave.
Well played! Few mistakes, plenty of good ideas. I'm proud of you.
Victory with style. Let's look at the moments that won it.

closeGame.text: A close one! A few small moments decided it. Let's look at them.
That was tight. You held your ground well. Here's where it turned.

toughLoss.text: A tough loss, but every hero falls before they rise. Let's learn from it.
Not our day. Still, I saw good ideas. Let's find the turning point together.
Losing hurts, but one lesson from this game makes the next one better.

keyMoment.text: This was the turning point. {bestMove} would have kept us on track.
Here's the key moment. Our {piece} on {square} needed more care.
Remember this one: {bestMove} was better by {loss}.

inaccuracy.text: Not bad, Summoner. A little loose, though. {bestMove} was tidier.
A small thing. Barely a scratch. {bestMove} would have kept more pressure.
Close enough for most, but you're better than most. Try {bestMove}.

mistake.text: Hm. That gives away {loss}. {bestMove} would have held things together.
A misstep. Don't fret, I've made worse for centuries. {bestMove} was better.
That costs {loss}. Let's look at why, calmly. I'm always calm.

blunder.text: Ah. That one drops {loss}. Shall we take it back and try {bestMove}?
Oof. Even I flinched, and I have no nerves. Undo, and look again.
A big slip. The living do it all the time. {bestMove} was the move.

good.text: Good move. Sensible. My bones approve.
Nicely played, Summoner. Solid as a tombstone.
That's a good one. Keeps everything in order.
Well done. You're learning faster than I did. I had more time.

best.text: The best move available. I'd applaud, but it's very clattery.
Exactly right, Summoner. Nothing better on the board.

brilliant.text: Brilliant. A sacrifice with a purpose. I felt that one in my marrow.
Remarkable. In four hundred years I've seen few moves like that.
Oh, that's wicked. In the nicest way. Bravo, Summoner.

fork.text: Mind {square}. Their {attacker} can go there and attack two of our pieces at once.
This allows a fork. Their {attacker} hits your {target} and another piece together.
One attacker, two targets, and we can only save one. Let's avoid that.
A fork. Your {piece} attacks two pieces at once. They can only save one.

pin.text: Your {target} is pinned. Move it, and something more valuable behind it falls.
Their {attacker} has your {target} stuck in place, like a bone in a museum case.
Careful on {square}. That {target} is pinned and can't help defend right now.
A pin. Their piece is frozen in place. I do enjoy a frozen piece.

skewer.text: A skewer. Their {attacker} hits your {target}, and the piece behind it falls next.
Your {target} and the piece behind it share one line. Their {attacker} likes that.
A skewer. The big piece steps aside, and the one behind it is ours.

hanging.text: Your {piece} on {square} is undefended. Their {attacker} can take it for free.
Nobody guards your {piece} on {square}. Lonely pieces don't last long.
That leaves your {piece} on {square} alone. Give it a friend or move it.

backRank.text: Our back rank is weak. The king has no escape square, so a rook could mate.
Give the king a window. One pawn step in front prevents a back rank surprise.
Back rank threat. Their king is boxed in by its own pawns. Cosy.

missedCapture.text: Their {target} on {square} was free to take. Always look for loose pieces.
There was a free {target} on {square}. Before each move, check every capture.
{bestMove} would have won {loss}. Their {target} had no guard.

allowsMate.text: Careful. After that, they can checkmate us. {bestMove} keeps the king safe.
That move lets them mate. I'd rather not lie down just yet. Shall we undo?
Danger. Their {attacker} has a checkmate coming. Let's take that back.

missedMate.text: You had a checkmate, starting with {bestMove}. Always look at checks first.
Nearly. {bestMove} led to mate. Next time, try every check before anything else.
A win was waiting after {bestMove}. Look at checks, then captures, then threats.

trappedPiece.text: Your {piece} on {square} has no safe squares. They can win it now.
That {piece} is boxed in. Even the dead need a little room.
You trapped their {target}. It has nowhere safe to go. Delightful.

discovered.text: Look out. When their piece steps aside, the {attacker} behind it hits your {target}.
A hidden attack. One enemy piece moves and the {attacker} behind it strikes.
A discovered attack. One piece moves, the one behind strikes. Very sneaky.

threat.text: Before you move, Summoner: their {attacker} has its eye on your {target}.
They're threatening your {target} on {square}. What shall we do about it?
Their last move had a purpose. Can you spot what their {attacker} wants?

hangingPiece.text: Your {piece} on {square} has no defenders. Lonely. Maybe help it?
Quick check: is your {piece} on {square} safe? I count nobody guarding it.

castleSoon.text: I'm still in the middle of the board. Draughty. Shall we castle soon?
Castling tucks the king away and wakes up a rook. Two birds, one bone.

developPieces.text: Some of our knights and bishops are still in their coffins. Bring them out.
Every piece should join the party before anyone goes adventuring.

controlCentre.text: The centre is the best real estate. Better than a hillside crypt, even.
Pieces in the centre see more of the board. Claim it early.

kingSafety.text: My guard is thin. Perhaps shore up the pawns around me?
Their pieces are gathering near me. Careful with the pawns in front.

endgameKingActive.text: Endgame now. The king can fight. Walk me forward. Slowly, mind my hips.
Few pieces left, so the king is strong. Bring it toward the centre.

wellPlayed.text: A fine game, Summoner. Clear moves, few errors. Even I'm impressed.
Well played. If I had cheeks, they'd be glowing with pride.
A stylish win. Let's look back at the moments that sealed it.

closeGame.text: A close one. Small moments decided it. Let's dig them up.
Tight game. You held on well. Here's where it turned.

toughLoss.text: A tough loss. I've had many. They make the wins taste better.
Not our day. Still, there were good ideas. Let's find the turning point.
Losing stings. One lesson from this game will make the next one better.

keyMoment.text: Here the game turned. {bestMove} would have kept us on track.
The key moment. Our {piece} on {square} needed more care.
Worth remembering: {bestMove} was stronger here, by {loss}.
